correctness.rationale: Independently re-proved Lemmas 1-3: u-marked per-size product with truncation to <=l parts is correct; e_i and h_j evaluations and partial-sum identity are standard and correctly applied; Chu-Vandermonde evaluation of L_z and polynomial continuation from integer r to all complex z is valid. Twin follows since conjugation preserves distinct part sizes (exhaustively checked for l,m<=4). Independently recomputed definition vs formula for 8 (l,m,z) cases including half-integers, all exact matches, and reproduced witness A(3,4,3)=(1,3,6,12,18,24,28,28,25,19,12,6,3). Corollaries at z=1 and z=0 check out.

originality.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING about the exact target object. Two consolidated literature searches plus full-text inspection of the nearest candidates (Kronenburg q-binomial sums, Melczer-Panova-Pemantle rectangle asymptotics, Yee Andrews-Stanley finite refinement, Pak survey Sec 2.4, Bridges bounded distinct parts, Ballantine elementary-symmetric partitions) show all use different statistics (exactly-m distinct parts, odd parts, k-measure/Durfee, unrestricted gamma) or different questions (asymptotics), and none states or implies the binomial(z-1,i) q-convolution expansion (*). No broader census, database, or dual encoding covers the claim.

value.rationale: Proved closed-form structural theorem for the exact target object: first Gamma-deformed corner-weighted q-binomial expansion unifying Gaussian binomial at z=1 and collapse to 1 at z=0, with nonnegative weights at integer z and an honest blocking analysis reducing open unimodality to staggered-centre sums. Object and invariant were motivated before computation, value is not known or mechanically implied, and a future researcher could need the precise generating function. Eligible new theorem under STANDARD, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, or unexplained enumeration.

broader_coverage.evidence: Melczer et al. give sharp asymptotics for N_n(l,m) and Kronecker differences; Yee gives finite Andrews refinement by odd-part numbers r,s with modular q^4 generating functions; Lin et al. give k-measure/Durfee-side refinements. claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Kronenburg identities (1.8)-(1.11) are double sums over P(n,m,p)/Q(n,m,p) with alternating signs and q-power shifts, proved from (1+zq^j)/(1-zq^j) manipulations; the submitted proof instead uses a truncated per-size product, staircase e_i evaluation, and Chu-Vandermonde evaluation of L_z. No substitution of parameters turns the former into the binomial(z-1,i)-weighted staggered q-binomial sum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Implication requires the prior conclusion to logically yield (*), possibly after routine specialization. The prior identities enumerate exactly-m (distinct) parts with fixed q-powers, while (*) weights by arbitrary function of the number of distinct sizes via L_z; neither statement implies the other.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Nearest q-binomial summation identities involving distinct partitions in a rectangle (Kronenburg 2206.05062 Theorems 3.1-3.3, equations 1.8-1.11) tested for logical implication of the claimed expansion.
